conditioningLevel.evidenceScope: Above-tail segment (ranks 1-9) of the exact-market INCI; formula-only structural position.
conditioningLevel.rationale: All three section 9.1 structural signals are satisfied on a nine-entry above-tail segment, which is the strongest structural configuration the rule can register. E2 ceiling: architecture, not delivered conditioning.
evidenceSignals: S1 satisfied: CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (6) and BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE (9) - two distinct long-chain cationic species above the tail
S2 satisfied: CETEARYL ALCOHOL at rank 2, immediately after AQUA
S3 satisfied: GLYCINE SOJA OIL (3), BUTYROSPERMUM PARKII BUTTER (5), COCOS NUCIFERA OIL (7) - three distinct non-fatty-alcohol lipids above the tail
Not counted (tail-side): HYDROXYPROPYL GUAR HYDROXYPROPYLTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (13), the two hydrolysates (15, 17), PANTHENOL (11)
Not counted (family 10 rheology/emulsifier): GLYCERYL STEARATE SE (14)
conditioningLevel.derivation: Section 9.1 S1/S2/S3 counting on the above-tail slice; signal count 3 of 3 -> high.
thresholdReasoning: Why high, not moderate: moderate covers zero or one satisfied signal plus the unresolvable fallback. Three signals are satisfied, each on independent evidence families (cationic breadth, fatty-alcohol rank, lipid breadth).
Why high, not low: low requires none of the three; every leg of the low anchor is falsified.

The 'no material counter-signal' clause was tested: the only counter-signals present (GLYCERYL STEARATE SE as a lipid-looking emulsifier, the tail-side protein cluster) are exactly the items the false-signal register neutralises, not blocking evidence.
counterSignals: GLYCERYL STEARATE SE reads lipid-like but is an emulsifier (lexicon family 10) - zero credit
Tail-side protein cluster is a sub-1% hero tail - zero credit in either direction
The 20 ml sachet format means a single-use dose, which is protocol/packaging information and carries no classification credit
limitations: Section 9.1's honest limitation: no published dataset maps INCI patterns to validated low/moderate/high thresholds; these anchors are provisional.
Confidence high is justified by three converging independent signals on a resolved tail with a complete exact-market list - the configuration the section 9.1 confidence rule names.

weightPotential.rationale: The required rich base is present and two independent R4b heavy lipids sit high above the tail, so this is the clearest weight-high anchor in the set. E2 ceiling: inferred, never measured; this is a matching prior, not a prediction of visible flattening.
evidenceSignals: Required base leg 1: >= 2 distinct cationics above the tail - CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (6), BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE (9)
Required base leg 2: cetearyl-class fatty alcohol in the top three - CETEARYL ALCOHOL (2)
Supporting alternative (a): BUTYROSPERMUM PARKII BUTTER (5) - a butter, the lexicon's heavy band; and COCOS NUCIFERA OIL (7), named in the standard's own R4b heavy-triglyceride list
Supporting alternative (b) absent: no silicone species anywhere in the list
weightPotential.derivation: Section 9.2 anchors as ruled 2026-09-04: base (two required markers) plus at least one alternative. Base + alternative (a) -> high.
thresholdReasoning: Why high, not moderate: the residual bucket applies only when the base or every alternative fails. Both hold, and alternative (a) holds twice over on independent species.
Why high, not low: all three legs of the low anchor fail (two cationics, cetearyl at rank 2, two heavy lipids above the tail).

Conflict fallback not applied: no exact-product lightness positioning is available in the packet, and nothing in the directions claims a light finish, so there is no conflict to resolve down to moderate.
counterSignals: No silicone at all - silicone-free is not evidence of lightness (section 9.2 counter-signal list)
The heavy lipids sit at ranks 5 and 7, above the tail, so this is not a decorative-butter false positive of the kind the lexicon flags on tail-side shea
limitations: Rank is used qualitatively only; nothing here supports a statement about how much butter or oil is actually present (Art. 19 semantics).
weight_high_conflict trigger is not fired because no lightness positioning was available to conflict with; a claims source could change that.

careDirection.evidenceScope: Above-tail vs. tail segments; comparative emphasis only, never a user-state assertion (G6).
careDirection.rationale: This is the discrimination case the standard is built for: a product named 'SOS Protein Treatment' whose only two protein species sit in the tail. With no qualifying R5 route above the tail, the material direction is the conditioning/emollient base the formula actually carries. E2 ceiling; no moisture-delivery claim is made.
evidenceSignals: HYDROLYZED VEGETABLE PROTEIN (15) and HYDROLYZED SWEET ALMOND PROTEIN (17) - both at/after the tail marker (10), zero credit
Zero R5 species above the tail

LACTIC ACID (18) and CITRIC ACID (20) are tail-side pH context, not actives (lexicon C3)

thresholdReasoning: Why moisture, not protein: the material-R5 test needs a qualifying species above the tail before either of its two legs can be evaluated. There is none. Section 9.3's counter-signal line - protein naming with the protein only in the tail resolves to moisture, claim recorded - is exactly this case.

Why moisture, not balanced: balanced needs the material R5 route plus a humectant cluster or S3. S3 is satisfied here, but the protein precondition is not, so balanced is unreachable. This matters: a reviewer who mis-scored the tail-side proteins would land on balanced on the S3 leg alone.

Confidence high: resolved tail marker, complete exact-market list, unambiguous route separation, and the D4 protein-payload cap does not engage because no R5 species is above the tail or in the top five ranks.

limitations: No claims summary. Claims are barred from care_direction anyway (section 11 step 4), so the value is unaffected; only the recorded claim context is thinner than it should be.

thresholdReasoning: Why general, not moisture: the D5 guard is missed by exactly one cluster member. Note the calibration signal: PANTHENOL is at rank 11 against a tail marker at 10 - one rank the other way and this product would have cleared criterion 1.

Why general, not curl_support: this is the case where I most wanted a claims source. The brand identity is curl-oriented, but step 3 is explicit that curl positioning is corroboration only and never creation, and the formula leg (high slip beyond baseline) is not met - the slip route is the ordinary two-cationic mask base. Curl-brand identity against a baseline slip architecture
